best_for: People who want a free browser that isn't built on Chromium, including Linux users who want a Flatpak that Mozilla itself publishes.

points.title: Privacy is the pitch
points.text: Mozilla highlights Total Cookie Protection, tracker blocking, Tab Groups, a built-in PDF editor, Sync across mobile and desktop, and a free password manager.

points.title: Older systems stay on ESR
points.text: Windows 8.1 and macOS 10.14 and older are pointed to Firefox ESR 115, the long-term support branch, rather than the current release.

points.title: Linux has several official routes
points.text: Mozilla offers 64-bit and ARM64 tarballs and an APT repository for Debian and Ubuntu. The Flatpak on Flathub is published by Mozilla and marked verified, for x86_64 and aarch64.

points.title: Enterprise is a separate product
points.text: Firefox Enterprise is an on-premises offering with central policy control and data-loss prevention, plus its own support tiers. Prices were not shown.

points.title: Three Windows architectures
points.text: Windows gets x86, x64 and Arm64 installers, installed machine-wide.

points.title: Long Windows history, thin elsewhere
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 183 versions. Mac and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades on those systems need another source.
